clue.text: Rugby players upset club, one making unwelcome suggestions

parts.note: the backs are the players behind the scrum in rugby
to eat someone is to bother them, as in 'what's eating you?'
a driver is a golf club used off the tee

explanation.surface: Rugby players are annoyed at their club, with one of them offering unwanted advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal for club, but it is a verb meaning bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting behind the driver who keeps telling them how to drive, extended to any meddling critic offering unwanted advice.

clue.text: Rear ducks to be restricted in the air

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: aft is the rear part of a ship
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O letters

explanation.surface: Ducks at the back must be stopped from flying.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, shaped like O; the two Os sit inside AFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that are underway or brewing are said to be in the air or afoot, both idioms for happening.

clue.text: Comedian's demise unusual: topped by butt of wisecrack

indicators.note: in a down entry, being topped by something means it sits above, so that letter comes first
the butt of something is its thick end, so only the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
a demise is an end
odd means strange or unusual

explanation.surface: A comic's death was strange, capped off by the target of a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'topped by' puts the K at the top. Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian from Liverpool, known for his tickling stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd was a celebrated English stand-up comic, so he is an example of the defined category.

clue.text: What is 2+5 if you subtract 1 at the start?

definitions.text: What is 2+5 if you subtract 1 at the start?

indicators.note: taking away one character from the front means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: two plus five is seven

explanation.surface: A puzzled child working through a sum, told to take one away first.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the S off SEVEN leaves EVEN; read as arithmetic, (2-1)+5 makes six, which is also even, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtracting one from the first number gives six, a number divisible by two, so the result is not odd.

clue.text: Unspeakable filling from fajita book

indicators.note: a filling sits inside, so the letters are found within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something too awful to mention was stuffed in a wrap, according to a cookery book.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo subject is one that must not be mentioned, so it is literally not to be spoken of.

clue.text: Red rose transformed decoration in church

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A red rose has been made into an ornament for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or panel behind an altar, a church furnishing.

clue.text: Wrongdoing against Nebraskan periodically? On the contrary

parts.note: vice is immoral conduct
v is short for versus

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of this word

explanation.surface: A crime committed against someone from Nebraska, now and then? Not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the other way round, so it reverses a statement just as the defining phrase does.

clue.text: "Thoughtless repetition," lecturer's marked on paper

indicators.note: a lecturer speaks to an audience, so we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: to mark on paper is to write, past tense wrote

explanation.surface: A lecturer has written 'mindless repetition' on an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W disappears when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means mechanically repeating material without understanding, hence mindless parroting.

clue.text: Toast? That is a delicious snack

parts.note: to toast bread is to brown it
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est

explanation.surface: Someone praising a piece of toast as a tasty nibble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like the definition of a snack, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small square of rich chocolate cake, a sweet treat eaten between meals.

clue.text: Mount champion horse?

parts.note: to best someone is to beat them, as a champion does
slang for something you ride, here a horse; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: Is this winning horse the one to get on?
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to sit astride, legs either side, as when climbing onto a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Child not quite right having eaten school soup

indicators.note: something that has eaten another holds it inside
not quite complete means falling short by the final letter

parts.note: a boy is a male child
RT is a standard abbreviation of right
SCH is the abbreviation of school

explanation.surface: A child, not quite behaving properly, has eaten some school soup.
explanation.walkthrough: RT is a common abbreviation for right, and the two parts of it are split around the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is a beetroot broth from Eastern Europe, especially Ukraine and Russia.

clue.text: Father Ted maybe to meet Catholic order

parts.note: a committee or court sits when it meets
C is a standard abbreviation of Catholic
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A priest called Ted might go to meet a Catholic religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Ted' looks like a priest, but it is the title of a TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Ted was a popular Channel 4 situation comedy about Irish priests, so it is an example.

clue.text: Cast finished broadcast in European country

parts.note: a cast is a mould, spelt mold in American English

indicators.note: something broadcast goes out over the airwaves, so we go by its sound

parts.note: finished means over; in non-rhotic speech it is said like ova

explanation.surface: A show's cast has completed a broadcast in a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a landlocked state in Eastern Europe between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: Corporation's put up indecent material

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: corporation is old jocular British slang for a big belly, a tum; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A corporation has published obscene content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is the old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or lewd writing or pictures, the kind of matter considered offensive.

clue.text: Impeach President, ultimately turning decisive

indicators.note: turning things over and around changes their order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the preceding word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A call to impeach the President, which proves conclusive in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means forceful and unambiguous, so a result described that way is clear-cut and conclusive.

clue.text: Shot that takes golfer hours

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single bullet or shell of ammunition
second meaning: a full game of eighteen holes on a course

explanation.surface: A golf stroke that takes the player hours to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a golf stroke, but it is a unit of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a cartridge for a gun and also a complete game of golf, which lasts several hours.

clue.text: You and me, every evening, entwined? That's revolting!

indicators.note: things entwined are twisted together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: you and I together are us
nightly means happening every night

explanation.surface: A couple wrapped round each other every night, to someone's disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means ugly or unpleasant to look at, so it is disgusting in a mild sense.

clue.text: Eddy West, dead in France, knocked over by Lexus on vacation

parts.note: Mae West was a famous American film actress

indicators.note: a place on vacation is emptied, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mort is French for dead

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy West died in France after being hit by a Lexus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name, but it is a swirl of water. 'By' means next to: the reversed word sits beside LS.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a large swirling current in water.

clue.text: Lubed up Greek scored no problem

indicators.note: scored out means crossed through, so those letters are removed

parts.note: lubricated with oil, slippery
GR is the abbreviation of Greek

explanation.surface: A well-oiled Greek scored without difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lubed up' might suggest a reversal in a down clue, but it is simply a synonym phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is easy, or no problem, means it is simple and causes no difficulty.

clue.text: He thought he was mad, asserted leader of council

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone convinced he was mad told the head of the council so.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to 'I think, therefore I am', the philosopher's famous proof of his own existence.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes reasoned 'cogito ergo sum', that thinking proved his existence, so he thought and therefore he was.

clue.text: Foreign actor accepting of French style

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters take an unfamiliar order
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the letters of this word rearranged
de is French for of

explanation.surface: An overseas actor adopts a French way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative design movement of the 1920s and 30s with bold geometric forms.

clue.text: Husband against underwear that's showy

indicators.note: against can mean pressed up beside, so one piece is set right next to the other

parts.note: bras are items of women's underwear
H is the abbreviation of husband

explanation.surface: A husband objects to lingerie he finds too flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' means placed next to, so H sits beside the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means loud and self-assertive, flashy in a vulgar or attention-seeking way.

clue.text: Extend course flanked by Scottish mountain

indicators.note: something flanked has company on both sides, so it sits within the other piece

parts.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a route or course

explanation.surface: Extending a route that runs between Highland peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To broaden something is to widen or expand it, making it reach further.

clue.text: A soldier thanks those exhausted in campaign

parts.note: taken as written
a GI is an American soldier
ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: something exhausted is emptied out, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A soldier thanks the comrades who wore themselves out on a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to press publicly for a cause or change, which is what campaigners do.

clue.text: Fish in river caught by hawk

indicators.note: something caught is held fast inside, so this letter goes within the other word

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them, selling aggressively
R is the abbreviation of river

explanation.surface: A fish in a river snatched by a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird, but it is a verb meaning to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Miscellaneous collection of biblical characters

parts.note: Job is the patient sufferer of the Old Testament
Lot is Abraham's nephew, whose wife became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: An assortment of people from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'characters' covers two figures, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed batch of goods sold together at auction, an assortment of odds and ends.

clue.text: Check statement of one chasing after lecturer

parts.note: L is the abbreviation of lecturer
the chaser in the game of tag announces 'I'm it'

explanation.surface: A check on what someone says while pursuing a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the chaser's words below L in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict or restrain it, which is what checking it means.

clue.text: Unknown animal noise repelled fly

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: A mystery creature's cry drove off an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move very fast, especially through the air, as when an aircraft flies.

clue.text: Hairy creature besides Coot

parts.note: yet means in addition, as in 'yet another'
Coot is the setter, who refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A furry animal alongside a coot, the water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coot' looks like the bird but is the name of this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a legendary shaggy ape-like being of the Himalayas.

clue.text: July? I must avoid motorway — it's busy

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: July is an example of a month; the question mark flags the example
ego is Latin for I, the self
M is the abbreviation for a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: In July I must keep off the motorway because the traffic is heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone constantly moving from one task to the next is active and occupied, an idiom for busy.

clue.text: Common disease to wipe out wild mice

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; 'disease' describes what it is typically applied to

parts.note: to end something is to finish it off

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled and disordered, so the letters run in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A widespread illness that could wipe out wild rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic illness is regularly found among a particular people or region, so it is prevalent there.

clue.text: Can nuns act in time over contaminated food warning?

parts.note: may and can both express permission

indicators.note: contaminated means polluted or spoilt, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation of time
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation of over

explanation.surface: Could nuns respond in time to tainted food with a warning?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin of food, but it is a verb meaning may.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase appears on packaging to alert people with allergies that traces of the allergen could be present.
